claims.summary: For any field F, D>=2 and proper degree-D pseudoideal J, E_D=direct sum_{i=0}^D P_<=i/(J intersect P_<=i), with graded products zero above D, is a commutative unital algebra with nilpotent positive ideal and only idempotents0,1. For z=[1]_1, z^D is nonzero but localizing at z or imposing z=1 gives zero. If F is infinite and dim Q_D>=2 it has infinitely many unital subalgebras. For the minimal one-bit Boolean pseudoideal J={(x^2-x)g:deg g<=D-2}, E_D=F[z,X]/(X^2-zX,(z,X)^(D+1)), dim E_D=2D+1; its degree<=1 space A times degree<=D-1 space B spans E_D, dim span(AB)/dim B=(2D+1)/(2D-1), and full stabilizer still has no nontrivial idempotents.
